key_insight: A kernel-method analysis bounds RFM approximation and estimation errors through operator eigenvalues, linking convergence to activation regularity.
engineering_relevance: The theory helps assess how random-feature count, collocation-observation count, and activation smoothness constrain RFM accuracy for linear PDEs.
method: Relate finite-feature approximation in Sobolev norms and the PDE residual seminorm to kernel ridge regression.
Bound RKHS estimation error from finitely many noiseless collocation observations.
Combine lower bounds and derive algebraic or stretched-exponential eigenvalue upper bounds from activation regularity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical upper and lower bounds under stated assumptions, but no numerical benchmarks or datasets.
watch_item: The estimation analysis assumes noiseless collocation observations; robustness to noisy data is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: A Convergence Analysis of the Random Feature Method for Linear PDEs
